newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate halts fall on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate halts fall on profit-taking.

text.p: Overnight Cetes rates reined in earlier falls on what traders said was profit-taking, closing down 50 basis points at 26.90 percent on Wednesday.
"Rates had fallen enough, so dealers were content to step in to sell and take profits," said a trader.
The overnight rate fell to a low of 26.45 percent by midday.
Dealers noted the fact that the peso remained stable despite Tuesday night's plunge in primary rates helped secondary rates to continue on their recent downward trend.
Banco de Mexico assigned bellwether 28-day Cetes at 27.02 percent, a fall of 206 basis points from last week's rate.
"Primaries fell by more than was forecast, so we expected the peso to be under pressure, but it held steady and did not influence the secondary market," said a trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso ended 0.3 of a centavo firmer at 7.8725/7.8770 per dollar.
Traders expected secondary rates to remain stable for the time being.

"Dealers have taken positions expecting rates to hold steady, although they could fall again in the second half of December," one trader said. "The outlook for inflation next year is triggering optimism."
Overnight rates on bank paper fell 55 basis points to 28 percent.
Banco de Mexico earlier injected 7.434 billion pesos into the market to offset liquidity shortages, auctioning three credits assigned at between 27.85 percent and 28.01 percent.

Credit maturities for Thursday were estimated at 5.582 billion pesos and traders said liquidity could be further squeezed by an overplacement of 959 million pesos carried over from the primary auction.
